episodes.159502: With an area of high pressure centered over western Arizona, drier air filtering into western New Mexico resulted in a downtrend in storm coverage across that area on August 4, 2021. However, sufficient atmospheric moisture in addition to an upper-level low that tracked over northeastern New Mexico provided the necessary ingredients for another round of scattered afternoon thunderstorms that primarily favored central and eastern portions of the state. Shower activity rom the previous night and cooler daytime temperatures limited the amount of available instability, and thus, most afternoon thunderstorm activity was sub-severe. However, a brief severe thunderstorm near Maxwell did produce quarter size hail.
episodes.159531: Early afternoon thunderstorms that pushed offshore along the Treasure Coast produced several strong wind gusts.
episodes.159608: A weak disturbance crossed through West Virginia on the evening of August 3rd which prompted scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. One storm in particular resulted in downed trees in the town of Mount Clare and minor flooding in Shinnston.
episodes.159745: Residual monsoon moisture paired with daytime heating was enough to generate scattered showers and thunderstorms over the mountains of west-central Colorado. Some storms produced moderate to heavy rain which led to localized debris flows in Pitkin County.
episodes.159771: Afternoon storms produce strong marine wind gusts over Tampa Bay area.
episodes.161119: A surface front meandered across south Georgia. During the afternoon, a short wave trough moved overhead, which triggered locally heavy rainfall in storms that formed along the surface front over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.161634: A Tropical Upper Tropospheric Trough (TUTT) and near normal moisture combined with daytime heating and local effects to generate a line of heavy showers, affecting the San Juan metro area.
episodes.162351: An upper low off the coast of California continued to advect low level moisture into the forecast area. During the afternoon and evening, another shortwave moving across the region initiated convective activity over the Blue Mountains, that then pushed east across the Grande Ronde valley with severe hail.
episodes.162402: Showers and isolated thunderstorms associated with an area of low pressure moving northward along the coast produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.162405: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with an area of low pressure moving northward along the coast produced a gustnado across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.162440: Isolated to scattered storms occurred across the eastern mountains and plains, with the highest coverage noted over the far southeast plains. A diminishing trend with this development occurred on this day, however, a few storms did produce heavy rainfall with flash flooding.
episodes.162469: Moist southwest to west winds helped cause thunderstorms over the SE Gulf of Mexico during the morning of August 4th, which spread east across the South Florida peninsula and collided with the east coast seabreeze during the afternoon hours.
episodes.162711: Localized flash flooding occurred near Glen Haven and The Retreat in the Cameron Peak burn area.  Flash flooding also impacted a portion of the East Troublesome burn area on the 3rd.
episodes.162725: Several waterspouts were observed near the Lower Florida Keys in association with regenerating convective cloud lines.
episodes.162769: An area of low pressure moved through the area, producing heavy rain especially along and east of Highway 17 toward the coast. One to three inches fell over much of the rain, but as much as three to almost eight inches fell along the coast from Onslow county through Carteret, southeast Beaufort, and Outer Banks Hyde and Outer Banks Dare, from near Rodanthe south.

events.narrative: Spotter UN-114 relayed a report of ping pong sized hail east just east of La Grande, OR.

Heavy rain washed out a crossing along Miller Fork.  The two washouts cut off all access to several residents on Streamside and Corner Court.   The residents sheltered in place until all repairs could be completed.   The Black Creek culvert under Corner Court was also washed out in The Retreat.

Grand County experienced periods of heavy rainfall during the evening.  The commercial operation at Drowsy Water Ranch was heavily impacted. The Ranch began an evacuation of guests to predetermined safe facilities on the property in accordance with their emergency plans.

A band of moderate to heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms was moving through northeast North Carolina around 7 AM Wednesday morning, August 4. As the tail end of the system moved through Grandy, damage was reported at Flippers Convenience and Arcade. The damage included a couple of windows that were broken and a portion of the roof was removed. On the west side of Caratoke Highway, a video camera from Wiseguys Pies was able to capture the event. It showed a swirl of winds hitting the store with debris being flung, and a flash of light from a transformer. It was determined that a gustnado impacted the area.
More than 3 feet of water along Back Road, near the Ocracoke Coffee Company.  The road was impassable due to deep water.  Videos were posted on social media.
Cape Point Campground was 100% flooded.  Significant amounts of water on some areas near Cape Point.

Parts of Highway 12 flooded in the typical spots including Pea Island section of the seashore in what is called the Canal Zone. Flooding along the roads and roadside ditches in all the villages and in some locations between the villages. Staff described the roadway flooding as very dangerous.
Significant ponding of water along South Point Road.
Ocracoke Campground 75% under water.
Emerald Isle Public Works closed Reed Drive between East and West Sea View Drive due to high water.
Entrance to Wildwood neighborhood cover with up to 3 feet of water.  Road not passable due to high water.
Merrimon Road flooded just before Merrimon Church.  Water was acrdoss the road in five places outside of Jonaquins subdivision.

events.county: Hawk Channel From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A waterspout was observed about 7 miles south of Geiger Key, with additional waterspouts observed via the National Weather Service office webcams well southeast of Key West.  One of the waterspouts had a condensation funnel extending halfway from cloud base to the water surface with a spray ring visible.  The waterspouts drifted toward the north.
Mesonet site reported rainfall total of 6.76 inches since midnight. Rainfall total of 5.16 inches fell between 4 am and 10 am.
Water was overflowing a pond and covering the roadway near the intersection of Austin Street and Villa Court.
The AWOS at Sebastian Municipal Airport, KX26, measured a peak wind gust of 35 knots from the south-southwest.
A mesonet at Sebastian Inlet Pier measured a peak wind gust of 42 knots from the west-southwest.
Weatherstem mesonet at House of Refuge measured a peak wind gust of 37 knots from the west.
Flooding reported inside a residence in Calle 13 with intersection with Calle 4 near the Gabriela Mistral School.

events.county: Volusia-Brevard County Line To Sebastian Inlet 20-60Nm
events.narrative: Buoy 41009 measured a peak wind gust of 35 knots from the southwest.
Flooding reported along Calle 40SE in Urbanization Reparto Metropolitano.
Flooding reported in Calle Jupiter.
Trained spotter reported a 45 mph wind gust on span of Skyway Bridge.
WeatherFlow site XLID New Pass Shoal Light reported a 41 mph wind gust.
ASOS site KPIE St. Petersburg-Clearwater International Airport reported a 41 mph wind gust.

A wind gust of 50 knots (58 mph) was recorded by the WxFlow site XTKY at Turkey Point at 258 PM EDT, at a height of 65 feet above the ground. A wind gust of 38 knots (43 mph) was recorded 5 minutes earlier.
PORTS site MTBF1 Middle Tampa Bay reported a 43 mph wind gust.
PORTS site OPTF1 Old Tampa Bay reported a wind gust of 40 mph.
WeatherFlow site XSKY Skyway Fishing Pier reported a 53 mph wind gust.

events.county: Gulf Of Mexico From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To 5 Fathoms
events.narrative: A waterspout was observed a few miles northeast of the NWS office in Key West. No spray ring was visible. The waterspout was nearly stationary.
WeatherFlow site XTAM Tampa Bay Cut J reported a 42 mph wind gust.
WeatherFlow site XCBN Clam Bayou Nature Park reported a 41 mph wind gust.
Pitkin County Sheriff reported the closure of Independence Pass along Colorado Highway 82 between mile markers 47 and 72 due to mudslides.
Flooding at the intersection of Main street and Olive street. Water was deep enough to require traffic redirection from law enforcement.
A trained spotter near Maxwell reported quarter size hail from a brief severe thunderstorm that tracked southeast through the area.
Heavy rainfall of 1.22 inches.
Storm total rainfall was up to 2.77 inches. About 2 inches fell between 6-7 pm.
